Commentary.Commentary: The heat is on Afghanistan. First, their aim will be to score 275 to make India bat again and drag this game into Day 5. But they need to target small pockets - Drinks after Lunch, then till Tea and so on. The task of batting till Stumps today itself is a big one - but if they do achieve that and manage to bat for a good portion of the first session tomorrow, it will be a good fightback. Join us back at 1210 local (0640 GMT) for all the action from the second session...

One has got to feel for the Afghanistan bowlers. Pressure got to them. But they managed to stave off some of that. They bounced back from India being 280/1 at one stage to have them reeling at Stumps last evening, only to let them run away for a sprint this morning. Yamin Ahmadzai was the pick of the bowlers. He bowled with intent and ended up with a 3-fer but the others, including Rashid, were ordinary. The spinners did pose some threat last evening but that was it. Nothing in the other 3 sessions overall.

A decent total posted by India but as has been the everlasting concern, it has been built on the foundation laid by the top three. The middle order has not contributed much, which could be worrying against better oppositions. Save aside Hardik Pandya's knock, there was nothing much to write about once Rahul was dismissed.

The visitors managed to get rid of Ashwin fairly early this morning but then the last 3 wickets added 105. Hardik Pandya scored the bulk of those, as expected, carting the bowling to all parts. He made a quickfire 71 from 94 balls but then what hurt Afghanistan even more was Umesh Yadav's cameo of an unbeaten 26 from 21 balls, with 2 fours and 2 sixes.

Hard to be harsh on Afghanistan but a bizarre performance this morning. Asghar Stanikzai chose NOT to take the second new ball and as a result, he has allowed India possibly struggling to reach 400 at one point of time, to end up getting almost 500.

PITCH REPORT - Sunil Gavaskar and Simon Doull doing the observation say that the grass is still there on the pitch. That will hold the cracks together which will help batting. But, there is some cloud cover around and some moisture, which means there will be some assistance for the bowlers as well.

Murali Vijay is giving an interview to Simon Doull. The opener says he was mentally prepared for the game. Adds further that he tried to stick to his basics, spend more time in the middle and it went well for him. On Afghanistan's bowling, Vijay feels that they were bowling better to the right-handers and hence he took his time. He mentions he is generally not nervous when he is in the 90s and tries to enjoy the moment. Reckons that once the ball got older it started to turn a lot more and ends by saying he feels good after the ton he scored.
Before we proceed further, warm wishes to all of those celebrating Ramadan. A big weekend is coming up ahead and hopefully, you folks have a great time. Amen!

WEATHER REPORT - Most of the times, the ones above decide the fate of the ones below. Bright and sunny skies yesterday helped India while an overcast evening helped the Afghans. As of now, it is bright and sunny. Quote unquote my colleague Baba who is at the ground - 'Weather is pleasant, in fact the best I have seen in a while.' Well, it will be nice to have an uninterrupted game.

A hard-fought day it was. Afghanistan started cautiously, only to be thwarted into submission by a rampant Shikhar Dhawan. It looked like all India around Tea when the skies changed their mood and accordingly, fortunes changed. 347/6 looks a very good total by the batting side on Day 1 of a Test - but to recover from a mauling of 280/1 will give a huge boost to the fielding side. Who will momentum favour this morning? The answer will be clearer in a few minutes' time. Hello and a warm welcome to the second day of the one-off Test between India and Afghanistan in Bengaluru.

That ends proceedings on the opening day! Who was the better side? Was it the one which started well or the one which ended in a terrific manner? Momentum will say Afghanistan but India are in a great position. They will be confident with this score and aim to bowl well on this track which suddenly has got something for the bowlers. Weather will be the key though. Join us for all the action on Day 2 at 0930 local (0400 GMT) to see how the game turns and develops. Before that, you can catch all the action from the exciting second Test between Windies and Sri Lanka. ADIOS! TAKE CARE!

Shikhar Dhawan is having a chat with Simon Doull. The Indian opener says that it feels great to score a century in one session and did not know that he was the first Indian to score a century on Day 1 of a Test before Lunch. On being asked further, he smiles and says that when one can score a century in T20 cricket, why not in one session? Being a bit more serious, he says that he first focussed on the singles and twos and when he got in, started to play his shots. Further says that the main aim for him was to test his fitness. On his dismissal, he says that is not that disappointed as he reckons that it is better getting out playing a shot rather than off a defensive one. On the game situation, he says that 400 will be a very good score on this wicket and India will aim to reach that mark tomorrow and then pick up some wickets of the opposition.

From a position of dominance at 280/1, India slipped to 334/6 and the Afghans had come roaring back. Yamin Ahmadzai picked up 2 wickets overall but it was the spin of Rashid and Mujeeb which was causing problems for the Indian batters. After hammering the spinners for a major part of the day, they struggled to pick them in the final session. The rain certainly helped the Afghans more than the Indians.

The first half entirely belonged to India. Dhawan attacked the bowlers mercilessly and was assisted well by Murali Vijay. The duo scored centuries which was followed by a half century from Lokesh Rahul. But, then came the rain which proved to be of gain for the Afghans.

A poor start but a magnificent finish. Nerves might have got the better of the debutants for most of the day but while heading back to the dressing room, it will be the Afghans who will be smiling a bit more than the Indians. Kudos to their effort and spirit, especially in this final session.

Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Very full outside off, Karthik comes forward to defend but is beaten by the leg spinner this time.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover-point.
Dinesh Karthik walks in at number 6, replacing his skipper.

OUT! That is a real, real surprise! That really looked high but Hawk Eye thinks otherwise. A short ball, in line of the stumps, Rahane goes back to work it to the leg side but is beaten by the skid on the delivery. He is hit high on the knee roll and the ball lobs to first slip. Rashid appeals and appeals but umpire Reiffel stays put. Now, the bowler is adamant and wants the review. Captain Stanikzai agrees and the first thing which is checked is the inside edge. None. Now, the LBW is checked for and... surprisingly, Height is not a factor! Not even umpire's call! Well, well, well. Earlier in the morning, the LBW appeal against Shikhar Dhawan looked more plumb than this. Has the rain affected the bounce on the track? Hawk Eye shows three reds as the ball is projected to hit the top of middle. Rahane departs cheaply again. Finally, a wicket for Rashid Khan.
Review time again! Rahane is the man in question. It is for an LBW verdict...
On middle and off, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
Full and outside off, pushed to the off side.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Outside off, punched to the off side.

Huge shout for LBW. Turned down. Floated nicely outside off, Rahane comes forward to defend but misses and is hit on the pads. The bowler appeals but the umpire is interested in something else as he is closely observing where the ball is landing. There is a bit of a chat about the review but it is not taken. Replays detect a thick inside edge which explains where the umpire was looking - whether short leg had taken the catch or not.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
Goes back and works it through mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! That is way too short, on leg, halfway down the pitch in fact, Pujara rocks back and pulls it behind square leg for a boundary. The stand moves to 32.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Goes back and whips it wide of mid-wicket for a single.
Outside off, punched off the back foot watchfully.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Good shot. That will make Rahane feel better. He seemed to have been marooned for a while. Short and outside off, punched through the covers for a boundary!
Down the leg side, left alone.
Much slower in pace, outside leg, Pujara is early into his flick but then waits for the ball to come. Then adjusts and works it behind square leg for a single.
Similar ball, played towards short mid-wicket this time.
Much fuller, around off, defended in front of short leg.
Around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Another spinner. Mujeeb Ur Rahman to bowl once more.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
On middle and leg, flicked towards short leg.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Full and around off, pushed back to the bowler.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. They pick up a single.
Full and outside off, pushed towards cover.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid on.
The widest of the three balls, comfortably left alone. Ahmadzai is struggling to control his line.
Wider than the previous one, probably the bowler is expecting some inward movement but there is none in this case. Left alone with ease.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
On a length outside off, pushed towards mid off.
Change of ends for Yamin Ahmadzai.

Got to be joking. Light is fading quickly and the umpires have called for Drinks. Technically, we can go up to 1800 local time, but doubt whether we will see that happening. India are back in control after the early hiccups after the Tea and rain break and now, Pujara and Rahane seem determined to see the day through. The question is - how long will play continue?
On middle and leg, played to the leg side.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Outside off, pushed straight to point.
On middle, flicked straight to mid-wicket.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman.
Outside off, punched off the back foot.
Rashid Khan is back on.
FOUR! Another boundary! A long hop, this is pulled away disdainfully to the mid-wicket fence. 14 from the over!
FOUR! That is a superb shot. On a length outside off, Pujara opens the face of his bat and guides it between slip and gully to the third man fence! 300 UP FOR INDIA!
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. They manage to come back for the second.
Short and outside off, punched straight to cover.
Outside off, played straight to point.
FOUR! Loose ball. Short and outside off, Pujara opens the face of his bat and steers it behind point. No stopping that. The stand moves into double figures.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Outside off, this one is let through.

NOT OUT! The ball has gone off the shoulder. That looked out to the naked eye. But thank God for replays and reviews. A very good short ball, targeting the batsman, around middle and leg, Rahane looks to pull but is cramped for room. He is unable to play that shot and the keeper collects behind and appeals. Umpire Reiffel raises his finger and instantaneously, Rahane reviews. He indicates to Pujara that it hit his shoulder and replays confirm that in one look. Ultra Edge assists as well.
Caught behind? The umpire thinks so. Rahane doesn't. Hence the review...
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Outside off, quietly left alone.
Full and just outside off, solidly blocked towards the bowler.
Slightly shortish outside off, AR cuts it through cover-point for a run.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
On a length outside off, Ajinkya defends it to the off side.
This goes wider than the previous one, Rahane shoulders arms again.
Landed outside off, left alone.
Half volley outside off, driven through the covers for a single.
Asghar Stanikzai is into the attack.
Driven through mid off by the batsman.
Full again on middle, Rahane drives it to mid off.
Fuller in length and on middle, Rahane eases it to long on. The runs are now starting to choke here. A good passage of play for Afghanistan.
Landed outside off, left alone.
Full on middle, pushed back to the bowler.
Outside off, left alone.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
On a good length outside off, Pujara looks to work it to the leg side and gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
Full and outside off, pushed back to the bowler.
That is a peach. The ball is landed on a length outside off and Pujara gets across to defend. But then the ball shapes away a touch and beats him.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
Outside off, played straight to point.
FOUR! Short and wide, Rahane flays it through point and gets a boundary! Off the mark on the 11th ball.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Around off, defended watchfully.
Down the leg side, left alone.
Outside off, left alone.
Goes full this time in search of some swing. There ain't any. Pujara drives it to covers.
This time it is down the leg side, Pujara misses the flick and the ball goes to the keeper who does well to dive to his left and collect it.
Third leave in a row! Outside off, left alone.
Another one which is outside off, Pujara does not fiddle with it.
A little too wide outside off, Pujara need not play at those.
Lands it on a length around off, Pujara lunges and defends it.
Outside off, left alone.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Around off and outside off, watchfully defended.
Outside off, left alone.
Around off, watchfully defended.
Ajinkya Rahane walks in at number 5, replacing Rahul.

OUT! The stumps are a mess. Wickets from both ends and Afghanistan have picked up 2 scalps in the span of 3 balls. A length fractionally fuller than short, outside off, Rahul looks to cut but is too close to the ball. As a result, he gets a thick inside edge which shatters the stumps. A start from Rahul again, which is not converted.
Yamin Ahmadzai is back on.
FOUR! Off the mark straightaway! A half volley on off, Pujara casually flicks it through mid-wicket and gets going!
Cheteshwar Pujara walks in at number 4, replacing Vijay.

OUT! LBW! The decision stays! Umpire's call hands Wafadar his maiden Test scalp. The nut is a good one. It is landed on a length outside off and it comes back in a long way. Vijay gets a good stride forward and shoulders arms. Is hit on the pads and up goes Wafadar in an appeal. Umpire Gaffaney raises his finger in a flash and the Afghans are pumped up! A distraught Vijay takes the review straightaway without even consulting his partner. And... Hawk Eye shows the ball to be the clipping the top of off stump. Vijay walks off after shaking his head. Tough luck. But what a knock. Take a bow.
Given out LBW! But Vijay has taken the review...
The batsman was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
Down the leg side, Murali misses his flick.
Full and outside off, Vijay drives it through the covers and it almost reaches the fence. Mohammad Shahzad dives to his right and saves the boundary. Two runs taken.
Full and outside off, pushed through the covers for a single.
A wrong 'un to end the over, Vijay misses his flick and is hit on the pads. 9 from the over.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
FOUR! Fine way to bring up the half century! A short ball again, on middle, Rahul gets across and paddles it fine for a boundary!

FOUR! Poor fielding from Mujeeb hands Rashid a century with the ball. A short delivery, Rahul rocks back and pulls it through mid-wicket. Mujeeb Ur Rahman runs to his left, gets to the ball, dives but lets it through. Gets up with a sheepish look and does not meet the bowler eye-to-eye.
On middle and leg, the batsman looks to work it to the keg side but the ball takes the bottom edge, bounces down and hits him on the legs.
A googly to start. Around off, Rahul defends.
Outside off, coming in, left alone.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
Outside off, pretty wide, Murali slashes hard but misses.
On a length outside off, punched towards cover.
Around off, defended to the off side.

FOUR! Up and over! Century number 12 for Murali Vijay! Nerves? Says who? A short ball outside off, extra bounce, Vijay just leaps and cuts it over point for a boundary! Takes his helmet off and raises both his hands. He walks across towards Rahul and the pair does a synchronized jig. The dressing room stands up and applauds again. The 'Monk' is back.
Right then... Vijay on 99...
Full and outside off, pushed back to the bowler.
Around off, spinning in, worked towards short mid-wicket.
We are back, they are back, everyone is back, welcome back! The sun is shining brightly at the M.Chinnaswamy Stadium. Rashid Khan to continue his pending over. Rahul to face...

1530 LOCAL - The rain has stopped but it is heavily overcast. Add to that, the water left on the ground is way too much to be dried out soon. Umpires Chris Gaffaney, Anil Chaudhary and Paul Reiffel are having a chat with one another. Too many molecules of hydrogen have been combined with oxygen and the resultant output is not that favourable...

The rain has arrived again and the players start running towards the pavilion. The groundsmen with the covers are running onto the field. It is pouring down at the moment. Seems like we will be in for a longer delay this time.
The googly, Vijay picks it and with the turn works it towards mid-wicket and moves onto 99.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
A huge appeal! The leggie on leg stump. Vijay goes for the flick but misses to get hit on the pads. The players appeal but the umpire shakes his head.
Floats it up on off, Vijay defends it onto the ground.
The floodlights are on. It has gotten quite dark out there.
Angles this one into the batsman. Murali works it through mid-wicket and gets to the other end.
Hits the length hard on off, Vijay defends it on the front foot.
Length ball on off, Rahul pushes it towards covers and gets to the other end.
A bumper on middle, Rahul ducks under it.
Moves onto 97 with that single! Another ball which is on the shorter side. Vijay goes back and punches it through covers and gets to the other end.
Tucks it around the corner with the angle for a run.
Another wrong 'un on off. Vijay tries to defend but it goes off the inner half towards square leg.
The googly, Rahul tucks it around the corner for a run.

FOUR! This has been Rashid's story today. He has bowled at least one bad ball in every over. This is short and wide outside off, Rahul has all the time in the world to go back and cut it through point.

Tosses it up on off, Vijay defends it with his bat ahead of his pad. The ball goes uppishly through the silly point region and then towards covers for a run. Had there been a silly point in place, there could have been a chance.
Flighted ball outside off, Vijay lunges and tries to keep it out but it goes off the outside edge to the man at short third man.
Floats it up on off, Vijay prods forward and blocks it.
Rashid Khan will bowl from the other end.
FOUR! The 250 is up for India! Another bread and butter shot for Rahul. Short and wide outside off, Lokesh gets on top of the bounce and cuts it late through backward point.
Good length outside off, left alone.
Short again and outside off, MV rocks back and punches it through cover-point for a run. Quite a few fielders in the deep for Afghanistan now. Looking to stop the boundaries.
Back of a length on off, Murali punches it off the back foot to the man at covers.
Lands it on a length outside off. The break has not hampered Vijay's concentration. He keeps his eyes on the ball and makes a leave.

We are now ready to get underway. The Afghanistan players make their way out to the middle. Lokesh Rahul and Murali Vijay will continue their innings. Wafadar will continue his over. He has five balls to go...
1443 Local time - The groundsmen have done their job and now we are only 7 minutes from play to resume. The last session can go onto 1730 and we have close to 45 overs to go today.
1436 Local time - Good news folks! The covers and ff and it also seems brighter now. Also the drainage here is really good so if the rain stays away then the action should resume shortly.

1400 Local time - While it rains the umpires have decided to take TEA EARLY! Another session which has belonged to the Indians. They did lose Dhawan early to Yamin but then Lokesh Rahul along with Murali Vijay have stitched another 50-run stand of this innings. The former is nearing his half ton while the latter is just 6 short of his century. 90 runs have been added in this session and just like the first one it has come at a good pace. If play resumes after the break, wickets is the call for the hour for the visitors. Whereas, the home side will want to continue from where they left off.

Scratch what I wrote last. The rain has once again started to pour down. More covers have been brought in. This does not look promising. Not sure the inspection will take place if the weather remains the same.
The rain seems to have stopped but it is still overcast. Also the outfield is still wet and the covers are still out. The next inspection will take place at 1400 local time.

All of a sudden the rain has come down quite heavily! The umpires have called for the covers and the players make their way back to the pavilion. Let us hope we are not in for a long delay here and it is just a passing shower. There are chances of the umpires taking early tea.

FOUR! Full marks to the bowler but runs to the batsman. Full and on middle, it is tailing away. Vijay looks to work it on the leg side but gets a leading edge through the vacant third slip region and into the fence.
Wafadar is brought back into the attack. He was quite impressive in the first session. Can he provide the breakthrough?
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. They pick up a single. He moves into the 90s.
Works it towards mid-wicket. The batsman wants a run but seeing the bowler move towards the ball quickly, Rahul sends him back.
Goes fuller and on middle, Rahul drives it towards mid on for a brisk single.
Bowls this one slightly short and outside off, Rahul guides it through point. Shahzad in the deep makes a good stop and keeps it down to two.
The googly on off, Murali strokes it past the diving cover fielder for a single.
Floats it up on off, Rahul drives it through covers and gives the strike to Vijay.
FOUR! Once again bowls a bad ball and Nabi is dispatched! Half-tracker outside off, Vijay slaps it through point and moves onto 12 short of a ton.
Slower through the air, Vijay works it towards mid-wicket.
Uses his feet now and eases it down to long on and gets to the other end.

FOUR! Controlled shot but a risky one especially with a slip in place. Short and outside off, it is turning back in. Rahul goes back and cuts it fine through short third man for another boundary. He has scored quite a few runs in that area.
Loopy ball on off, Rahul pushes it to mid-wicket.
Tosses it up nicely on off, Rahul prods forward and blocks it.
Change of ends for Mohammad Nabi.
A good delivery to finish! A good over by Rashid. This is quicker and it is the leg spinner. Vijay goes back and tries to keep it out but is beaten by the bounce and the spin.
The batsman opens the face of the bat and helps it to short third man.
Works it with the turn, away from the short leg fielder and to the man at deep mid-wicket for a run.
Flatter outside off, guided to point.

Just short! The short leg fielder though is getting up a little too quickly. He needs to be low and that is exactly what Rashid is telling him. He bowls the googly on middle, Rahul goes back and works it towards short leg. It hits the fielder's leg on the bounce.
Very full on middle, almost a yorker. Rahul jams it out.
Rashid Khan is back on. Not been at his best today. Can he turn it around now?
Floated ball on off, Vijay drives it to mid off.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
FOUR! This is class by Vijay! Flatter and quicker outside off, Murali rocks back and cuts it late through short third man for a boundary.
Works it through square leg and gets to the other end.
Flatter but in line of the stumps, Lokesh blocks it.
Flighted ball on off, Rahul keeps it out.

Drinks! Another passage of play which has belonged to the Indians. The visitors did get the wicket of Dhawan after the break but Rahul then joined forces with Vijay and the two have managed to build another fifty-run stand in this innings.
FOUR! Innovation at its best! Brings out the reverse sweep, plays it fine through the off side for a boundary.
Pushes this against the turn through covers for a run.

Hesitation but safe! Rahul nudges it towards square leg and Vijay wants a run. He sets off but Rahul is not interested. Murali now turns and tries to get back in. The fielder collects the ball and has a shy at the bowler's end but misses. However, replays later on show, the dive would have saved MV.
Works it with the turn towards deep mid-wicket for a run. The 50-run stand between the two is up.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket.
The Indian batsman though are just too good to be kept quiet. Rahul here uses his wrists and works it through mid-wicket for a run.
A tight over by Mujeeb! He pushes this through on off, Vijay punches it to covers. They need to keep bowling a few tight overs and build the pressure on India.
Flighted delivery on off, it is driven to the man at covers.
Floats it up on off, MV defends it onto the ground.
Down the leg side, Vijay fails to put it away.
Fires it on middle, Rahul pushes it down towards mid on for a run.
Flatter outside off, Rahul guides it to point.
Works it with the turn to the man at mid-wicket.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Now off the back foot, he pushes it through covers and only gets a run.
FOUR! On the shorter side, Rahul goes on the back foot and cuts it through point for a boundary. The run flow is just not stopping here.
The batsman dances down the track and does well to block the ball.
It has started to drizzle! There was forecast of rain and it has arrived. However, it is not that heavy for the players to walk off.
Eases this down to long on with the turn and gets to the other end.
Flatter and on the stumps, kept out.
FOUR! Once again makes the mistake of bowling it very full. It is outside off, Rahul leans into it and times it through covers for the second boundary of the over.
Loopy ball on off, Rahul defends it onto the ground.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
FOUR! Lovely! Dances down the track also makes room. Gets to the pitch of it and strokes it through covers for a boundary.
Very full outside off, Vijay tries to sweep it but getting his pads outside the line of off stump. He misses to get hit on the pads. The ball rolls on the off side and the batsmen run a leg bye.
Mujeeb Ur Rahman is brought into the attack.
Floats it up on off, Rahul blocks it out.
Driven through the covers by the batsman.
Gives it air on off, kept out.
Slightly shorter on off, Vijay goes back and punches it down to long off for a run. 200 up for India.
Loopy ball on middle, Rahul drives it back to the bowler.
Flighted ball on off, Vijay lunges and defends.
Mohammad Nabi is into the attack.
Goes around the wicket and gives it air outside off, Murali eases it down to long off and retains strike for the next over.
Down the leg side, Vijay lets it be.
Fires it full on off, Rahul times it to mid off for a quick run.
The leggie this time on off, it skids through. Rahul does well to defend it onto the ground off the back foot.
Flighted ball on off, Vijay wrists it down to long on for a run.
The wrong 'un on off, Rahul picks it late but adjusts and works it fine on the leg side for a single.
Close! On a length outside off, Vijay goes after it away from his body with a cut shot. The ball however, whizzes past the outside edge.
Goes wide of the crease and angles it in on off, MV gets behind the line and keeps it out.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.

Outside edge but well short! Full and wide outside off, Rahul tries to hit it through covers. He gets an outside edge which goes on the bounce to the fielder at gully. He misfields and concedes a run.
Back of a length on off, it is pushed towards mid off for a run.
Fuller on off, it is eased to the man at mid off.

Was there an edge? It did sound so. This was full and outside off, very full I should say. Rahul tries to jam it out towards the off side. He misses. He hits the ground as the ball passes the bat. The keeper fails to collect it. Replays later on show there was no bat involved. The sound was of the bat hitting the ground.
Again, after bowling two decent deliveries, bowls a short one on the pads. The field is right as square leg is in the deep. Only a single results.
Attacks the stumps, the batsman keeps it out.
Loopy ball on off, defended towards covers for a run.

Lucky to get away there Rashid! This is another half-tracker down the leg side. Rahul swivels to pull but does not connect. He will be disappointed he did not get that away. That was begging to be hit.
Rashid once again bowls it short on middle, Murali whips it through mid-wicket. They have a man in the deep this time and only a single results.
The batsman has punched that ball through the off side.
Just like this one! He does not get a boundary but gets three. Fuller on middle, Vijay works it wide of mid on. Mujeeb there hares after it and saves a run for his side.
Good shot but finds the fielder! Full and on off, Vijay on the up, strokes it to the man at mid off. A little to his left or his right and that would have been another boundary.
Down the leg side, Rahul flicks it down to fine leg and gets to the other end.
Another ball outside off, left alone.
Good length outside off, Rahul lets it be.

FOUR! Stanikzai does bring in a mid-wicket but it makes no difference. The last one was a half-tracker and this one is a full toss. Vijay says thank you so much and he flicks it through that region for back-to-back boundaries.
FOUR! Once again it is on the shorter side. MV whips it through mid-wicket for another boundary through that region. Need to bring in a man there.
This is where Rashid has to bowl! Flighted ball on off, all Vijay can do is lunge forward and defend it.
Uses his wrists and works it down to mid on.
Loopy ball on off, Vijay digs it out back towards the bowler.
FOUR! Too short and Vijay pays the price. On middle and it is the googly. He rocks back and whips it through wide mid on. Mujeeb gives up the chase and the ball crosses the fence.
Goes fuller on middle, trying to hit the pads of the batsman. Rahul gets his bat down in time and works it to mid on.
On the shorter side outside off, Rahul thinks about cutting it but then on seeing the ball too close to play that shot, he opts out.
Attacks the off stump and Rahul is solid in defense.
Back of a length outside off, left alone.
Goes fuller outside off, a similar delivery to the way he got Dhawan with. Rahul however, times it well but finds the fielder at covers.
On a length around off, the batsman keeps it out.
Driven towards the mid on region.
On the shorter side but the ball skids off the surface. MV flicks it to mid-wicket.
Flatter and on the shorter side on leg stump. Vijay goes back and tries to flick but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Another loopy ball on middle, Vijay works it through mid on for a brace.

Fifty for Vijay. A very characteristic knock by him. He played second fiddle to Dhawan all this while but he would now look to take control and get to the three-digit mark. He flicks this full ball on the pads very fine on the leg side and gets two to reach to the milestone.
Works it with the turn to mid-wicket.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Good length on off, Rahul tries to defend but it goes off the inner half towards mid-wicket. The batsmen take a run.
Lokesh Rahul is the new man in.

OUT! Afghanistan get the breakthrough. It is Yamin who is the first Afghanistan bowler to take a Test wicket. The ideal start for them after the break. It is full and outside off, enticing Dhawan for the drive and the way he is playing he does not back out. Goes for it away from his body. The ball takes the outside edge and flies towards second slip. The fielder, Rahmat Shah, there, fails to hang on and the ball lobs up towards first slip. Nabi there shows great awareness and takes it easily. The visitors celebrate as they have the centurion. He does not add a lot to his tally after the break. The away side will now look to build on this.
Angles this one onto the pads, Vijay nudges it fine down the leg side for a run. 2 short of a half ton now.
On middle, worked towards mid-wicket and gets to the other end.
Starts off on a length around off, left alone.
Yamin Ahmadzai will bowl from the other end.

FOUR! Takes him to 47! Impeccable timing! This is floated up on middle, it is once again the googly. Murali uses his wrists and works it through wide mid on. Mujeeb gives it a chase but the ball wins.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Straightaway Dhawan is onto the attack. He uses his feet and slams it past the bowler. Stanikzai from deep mid on runs to his right and makes a diving stop. The batsmen take a run.
Better by Rashid. He floats this one up on middle, Murali eases it to mid on for a quick run. He moves onto 43.
On the shorter side, Dhawan has all time in the world to rock back and flick it through mid-wicket for a run.
Starts off with a delivery down the leg side. Vijay works it towards short fine leg for the first run of this session.
We are back after the break. Shikhar Dhawan and Murali Vijay will resume their innings. The latter will be on strike and he will be facing, Rashid Khan who start the proceedings.
... Day 1, Session 2 ...

Not a lot to write about the Afghan bowling. Wafadar was the most impressive as he troubled the batsman with the new ball but the spinners were all over the place. A lot was expected from Rashid, Mujeeb and Nabi but the three were guilty of either pitching it too short or bowling too full. The visitors now have to re-think their strategy and come back rejuvenated after the break or a resurgent Dhawan will probably take the game away from them. Will the carnage continue or will the away side's bowlers come to the fore? Join us in a while to find out.

What a session for India and Dhawan. He walks off to a standing ovation from the crowd. Stroke-making at its best. The two openers have justified Ajinkya Rahane's decision to bat first. They looked shaky at the start when the ball was doing a bit but once the ball stopped moving, it was a combination of both, poor bowling as well as excellent batting. No bowler was spared as Dhawan hit them all over the park. Yes, they did miss a review against him but take nothing away from the knock he has played. Also credit to Murali Vijay who has given him excellent support from the other end.
Full again, a watchful block to end the session. LUNCH ON DAY 1!
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Around off, watchfully defended back to the bowler.
Gets across, comes forward and pushes it towards long on for a single.
Around off, Vijay blocks it out again.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Mohammad Nabi is back on.
FOUR! Once again the sweep shot is played to good effect. He goes down on one knee and sweeps it away from the square leg fielder to end the over with two consecutive boundaries.

FOUR! Hundred for Dhawan, his 7th in Tests. First Indian to score it before Lunch on the opening day and the sixth overall. It has come up in just 87 deliveries and he gets there in style. This is tossed up on off, Dhawan leans into it and strokes it through wide mid off. The ball races away. He acknowledges the applause from the crowd. He would now want to make it a daddy one.
Eases it to mid on and gives the strike to the man who is on 96.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
FOUR! A gift, down the leg side. All Vijay has to do is get bat to it. He does so as he sweeps it fine through the leg side.
Flatter on off, this one spins away. Vijay goes back and tries to defend but gets beaten.
No, he can't. A dot to end. This is eased to the man at mid on.

FOUR! Three in a row! A boundary away from a ton now. Another short ball outside off, Dhawan cuts this through point and another boundary results. Runs are just leaking here. One more ball to go in this over, can he make it four in a row and get to his ton?

FOUR! He is toying with the bowler here! The last one was short and he expected this one to be full. He comes down the track and lofts it over the mid off fielder for another boundary. He moves into the 90s.
FOUR! Easy-peasy! Another short ball and there is width on offer outside off. Dhawan slaps it through covers. There is no fielder there and the ball reaches to the fence in no time.
The last ball forces the bowler to go short. Vijay rocks back and whips it through mid-wicket for a run.
FOUR! Effortless! Slightly fuller outside off, easy for Vijay. He plants his front foot forward and drives it through covers for a boundary.
A beauty to end the over! The googly on middle, this one turns and bounces. Dhawan from the crease tries to keep it out but is beaten. The keeper behind does well to collect it.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
The leggie, this one bounces a touch extra. Dhawan tries to clip it but is done in by the extra bounce. It hits him high on the pads.
Nudges it to the man at square leg.
The googly on middle, Vijay with the turn, works it through the leg side for a run.
Flatter and on off, Dhawan goes back and punches it to the man at mid off for a run.
Action replay of the last delivery.
Works it with the turn to the man at mid-wicket.
Quicker but on the shorter side, Vijay off the back foot pushes it back to the bowler.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Fires it on middle, Dhawan off the back foot keeps it out.
Flatter on middle, Dhawan works it to the man at mid-wicket.
The googly outside off, Vijay waits for the ball, lets it do its bit and then guides it towards short third man.
Another one which is slightly short on middle, Dhawan clips it towards short fine leg for a run.
Flatter on middle, MV nudges it through mid-wicket and gets to the other end.
Vijay works it with the turn towards short leg.
Floats it up on off, Vijay keeps it out.
The leg spinner on off, Vijay rocks back and tries to defend but is beaten by the away turn.

SIX! He is in 'I-don't-care-about-who-are-you' mode. Waltzes down the track, gets to the pitch of the ball and sends it wayyyy over long on. I thought when MS Dhoni lifted the trophy a couple of weeks ago, the Indian T20 League was over for this season.
Around off, watchfully defended.
Goes back and tucks it through mid-wicket for a single.
Outside off, pushed towards mid-wicket.
SIX! Now Vijay gets into the act. Full and outside off, the right-hander plonks his left leg down and sweeps it powerfully over mid-wicket!

Full and outside off, Vijay lunges to defend but the ball goes off the inside edge past short leg. Dhawan is halfway down the track but has to be sent back as not for the first time today, Vijay is caught napping. Dhawan makes it back in time.

NOT OUT! Going over! Did not see that coming but an excellent decision by the umpire. It is the leggie from Rashid on middle, it pitches and turns back in sharply. Dhawan plays down the wrong line and gets hit on the front pad. The ball flies towards Shahzad at first slip who dives to his right and takes it brilliantly. The players appeal for both an LBW as well as a catch but the umpire shakes his head. The players want it to be reviewed and Stanikzai signals the 'T'. Time for the replays and they show there is no bat involved and it is going over the stumps. Afghanistan lose a review.
Review time! It is their first in Tests. An LBW appeal has been turned down and Rashid wants it to be taken upstairs. They do. Looks pretty close.
FOUR! DEFT! 14 from the three balls. This is flatter and outside off, Dhawan waits for it and then guides it through short third man for another boundary.
SIX! Rashid is being taken to the cleaners here! Dhawan steps down the track, this time it is a tossed up delivery. Gets to the pitch of it and lofts it over the long off fence.

FOUR! All the battles in the nets between the two for Hyderabad are coming in handy for Dhawan here. Another googly and outside off, Dhawan picks it once again and slaps it through covers for a boundary.
Dhawan dances down the track but once again the length is a touch short and hence he does not get to the pitch of it. He strokes it to covers.
The googly again. Vijay works it with the turn through the leg side for a run.
The batsman has driven it through mid off.
A low full toss on leg stump, Dhawan sweeps but finds the fielder at square leg.
Fires it on the pads, Dhawan tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads.

Changes his pace and bowls it slower through the air, almost similar to the delivery he got Kohli with on this ground. Vijay though gets to the pitch of it and strokes it towards covers. Dhawan wants a run and goes for it. Murali is late in responding as the fielder has a shy at the bowler's end but misses. Vijay however, had made it in, in time.
Goes flatter on off, this one shoots off the surface. Vijay does well to keep it down off the back foot.
Driven through the covers by the batsman.
Mujeeb Ur Rahman is into the attack.

Goes around the wicket, not something you see a lot from Rashid. He fires it on the pads. Dhawan flicks it to short fine leg. 5 from this over of Rashid. He has gone for 19 in his three and India are cruising at an excellent rate here.
A yorker on middle, Dhawan jams it out.
FOUR! Brings the sweep out and plays it very well again. This is down the leg side. Dhawan sweeps it through backward square leg and there is no stopping those.
The googly on off, Dhawan keeps it out.
A full toss on off, Vijay mistimes it towards covers. The fielder, Rahmat Shah, there misfields and concedes a run.
Flatter on off, kept out.

FOUR! Crunched! Trademark Dhawan there. Slightly fuller on off, Shikhar plants his front foot forward and drives it on the up. Finds the gap between mid off and cover for a boundary. End of a long over by Wafadar, probably his last.
BYE! Signs of tiring here! The bowler is getting a touch wayward. This is down the leg side. Vijay misses the flick. The keeper does well to make a half-stop. The batsmen cross over.
Good change in length! This is probably the first bumper of the game. It bounces just a little to high as the umpire calls it a wide but good thinking by the bowler.
Back of a length outside off, Dhawan guides it behind point and takes a run.
Good shot but for no runs! Fullish and on off, Dhawan strokes it off the middle towards covers. The fielder there runs to his left and makes a good stop.
A little wide outside off, left.
Back of a length on off, defended.

No ball but a good delivery! From around off, he angles it into the batsman. It jags back in after pitching. Dhawan makes a watchful leave. The umpire signals a no ball as the bowler has overstepped. The crowd lets out a big roar but let me remind them, there is no Free Hit.
Another googly on middle, Vijay fails to pick it. He tries to clip but is hit on the pads. The players appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Going down leg for me. Hawk Eye confirms that later.
The googly, Dhawan once again picks it and pushes it through cover-point for a single. Dhawan seems to be picking his Indian T20 League teammate quite well.
This is a good comeback over by Rashid till now. The leggie and on middle, it skids through. Dhawan at the very last moment gets his bat down and defends it.
Uses his feet but does not get to the pitch of it. He keeps it out.
The googly outside off, it skids off the surface. Dhawan picks him and goes for the cut but is beaten.
Flights it up on off, Dhawan prods forward and defends it.

FOUR! Third shot in a row in that area and this time he finds the gap. That was full timing. Slightly shorter and outside off, Vijay punches it through cover-point for a boundary. Spoils what was a good over.
Shortish outside off, Vijay with an angled bat guides it to point.
Shorter in length outside off, guided to point.
Goes fuller but there is no swing available. Vijay hits it back with a straight bat. The ball hits the stumps at the other end and defects towards mid off.
Back of a length on off, defended onto the ground.
A good delivery but Vijay should have probably left that one! On a length and around off, it jags away after pitching. Vijay has a needless poke at it away from his body and gets beaten.
Wafadar is back on. Just an over's break for him.
On middle and off, watchfully defended. 13 from Rashid's opening over.

FOUR! Even worse from Rashid. This is a full toss - Dhawan just whips it through mid-wicket. Another boundary. A half century in 47 balls for the southpaw. He is looking in imperial touch. Three boundaries of the over already.
FOUR! That is a bad ball. Dropped in short, Dhawan goes back and pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary!
On middle and off, punched back to the bowler.
FOUR! Easily done. Jumps down the track, gets to the pitch of the ball and flicks it through mid-wicket for a boundary. Remember, Dhawan and Rashid play for the same team in the Indian T20 League.
On middle, Vijay taps it to the leg side and takes a quick single.
Here he comes... the rising star of Afghanistan. Rashid Khan into the attack.

Drinks! An interesting hour of play. Afghanistan started off well but once the Indian openers realized that there was nothing on offer, they started to open up. There was a chance of Dhawan which could not be taken. Maybe a review could have been used... but otherwise India well and truly on top.
Floats it up on off, Dhawan defends it onto the ground. End of an action-packed over.

Dances down the track again and tries to get past the man at short leg. Luckily for Dhawan it hits his leg and goes away from him. Had he collected it, there could have been a chance of a run out as Dhawan was way down the pitch.
FOUR! Dhawan loves using his feet to the spinners and he is very good at it. Gets to the pitch of the ball and slaps it through covers for back-to-back boundaries.
FOUR! That should release the pressure that was building! Dhawan sits down on one knee and sweeps it over square leg for a boundary.
Flighted ball on off, Dhawan defends it.

Another huge appeal! The arm ball around off, Dhawan pods forward and defends it with bat and pad close to each other. The players appeal as the feel it is pad first but the umpire does not agree. They have the option to take it upstairs but do not. Replays later on show it is pad first but the impact seems to be outside off.

Another excellent delivery! He is getting the ball to move both ways which is making the batsman to think. Another inswinger on off, Vijay once again adjusts late. Tries to defend it off the back foot but the ball hits him on the glove.
Gets this one to come back in from outside off. Vijay at the very last moment adjusts and keeps it out.

Once again bowls it in the corridor of uncertainty. Vijay is unsure whether to play at it or leave it. He decides to leave it at the very last moment but is a touch too late. The ball goes off the bottom edge to gully.
Hits the length hard on off, Vijay defends it on the back foot.
Beautiful! He has been brilliant in his last two overs. Once again comes running in and angles it into the off pole. Gets it to leave the batsman. Vijay pokes at it and gets beaten.
Fuller in length on off, Vijay strokes it to mid off.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Another half-tracker outside off, Vijay pushes it towards covers and gets to the other end.
FOUR! Swept and swept fine! Vijay goes down on one knee and hits it through backward square leg. 11 from the over so far. 50 up for India.
Slightly on the shorter side, Dhawan works it around the corner and gets to the other end.
Flatter on off, Dhawan keeps it out.
SIX! Excellent use of the feet! Gets to the pitch of it and hits it straight over the bowler's head for a biggie. First of the game.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman. One run added to the total. End of an excellent over.

Howzat? Not out is the answer to that question. Another top nut! On a length, angles into the batsman first due to which he has to play at it. Straightens after pitching. The ball seems to have missed the outside edge as it goes into the mitts of the keeper. He though takes it and appeals. The umpire though shakes his head. Stanikzai has a long chat with his teammates and then opts against the review. Hang on now! Later on Snicko shows a spike as the ball passes the edge. An opportunity goes abegging there. How costly will this prove?

Good bowling this! He kept taking the deliveries away. This time he brings it back in. Dhawan is surprised by it. He plants his front foot across and goes for the flick but misses to get hit on the pads. The players appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Going down with the angle.
Third leave in a row! Outside off, the batsman does not fiddle with it.
This is nicely bowled! On a length and angling into the batsman first. Leaves him a touch late. Dhawan first thinks of playing at it but then shoulders arms to it.
Changes his angle and comes around the wicket. The line again is outside off and on a fuller length. He wants the batsman to go for a loose shot. Dhawan resists the temptation and makes a leave.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Bowls it on the pads, Vijay lets it be. The ball hits his pads and goes down towards fine leg. The batsmen do not run as Murali had not offered a shot.

Dhawan makes use of his feet and strokes it towards covers. He sets off for a run immediately. Vijay however, is caught napping. He takes off late. The fielder collects the ball and fires it to the keeper but Murali makes it in, in time.
Slower through the air on off, Dhawan defends it off the front foot.
The arm ball on off, it comes in with the angle. Dhawan prods forward and keeps it out.
Starts off with a loopy ball on off, it is a touch too full so the turn is out of contention. Dhawan eases it to covers.
Spin introduced quite early! Mohammad Nabi is into the attack.
Back of a length again on off, Vijay guides it towards gully. The fielder there fumbles but does not concede a run.

EDGY FOUR! Vijay's edges are working overtime here. His second boundary behind the wicket. On a length and around off, this one shapes away a touch. Vijay lunges and tries to drive it on the up. The ball takes the outside edge, past the diving second slip fielder for a boundary.
Slightly straighter in line. Vijay tries to nudge it but misses to get hit high on the thigh pad.
Yes, he has an off side field but there fielders are of no use if you do not make the batsman play. Another delivery outside off, Vijay does what he has been doing until now. LEAVE IT.
Bends his back on this one and hits the deck hard outside off, Vijay watchfully lets it through to the keeper. The ball carries at a good height to the keeper.
Good length outside off, left alone.
Ahmadzai is seen walking off the field. The heat here is maybe getting to him as he makes a tired walk back to the pavilion.
Poor ball to end! Down the leg side, Dhawan lets it be. End of an expensive over, 13 runs from it.

FOUR! Third boundary in the over! Perhaps this once could have been stopped. But a poor delivery, on the pads. Dhawan works it towards fine leg. Mujeeb there runs to his right, dives but fails to stop it. Fifth boundary for Dhawan, he moves onto 22.
The batsman has punched that ball through the offside.
Pulls his length back and bowls it on off. Dhawan taps it to the off side.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries! Full and on off, Dhawan leans into it and times it through covers. India are dealing in boundaries here.
WIDE! Way outside off, Dhawan lets it be and the umpire signals it as a wide.
FOUR! A boundary to end the last over and one to begin this one. Full and on the pads, Dhawan flicks it over square leg and the ball races away.
FOUR LEG BYES! This time he errs in line and bowls it on the pads. Vijay misses out on the flick shot. It brushes his pads and goes fine on the leg side for a boundary.
Wafadar's first ball to the right-hander and he has no problem in adjusting. He lands it on a length and on off, Vijay defends it towards mid off.
Another decent delivery, on off and swinging away a touch. Dhawan tries to block but the ball goes off the inner half towards mid-wicket and the batsmen take a run.
Goes fuller outside off, enticing the batsman to drive. Dhawan does not shy away. He however, mistimes it to covers.
This is what the bowler should be bowling consistently. Hits it hard on a length and attacks the top of off. Dhawan off the back foot defends it to point.
Lands it on a length around off and slants it away. Dhawan lets it be.
5th leave in the over! Outside off, left alone.
Again, a little too wide outside off, Vijay will not mind shouldering his arms to such deliveries the whole day.
Closer to the off pole but not close enough to make the batsman play at it.
Fuller but the line is a touch wide outside off. It shapes away. MV makes a leave. Need to bowl it a touch closer to the off pole and then take it away.
FOUR LEG BYES! Goes wide of the crease and angles it on the pads. Vijay fails to clip but the ball clips the pads and races away to the fine leg fence.
Another length ball outside off, Vijay is in no mood to play at it.
A good finish to the over! A maiden. On a length and around off, kept out.
Another decent delivery! In the corridor of uncertainty. Dhawan does the right thing and does not play at it.
A better second over by Wafadar so far. Lands it on a length and attacks the stumps. Dhawan off the back foot, defends it to point. He thinks of a run but is sent back.
Down the leg side, Dhawan goes for the flick but misses. The ball brushes his pads and goes to the keeper who does not collect it cleanly.
Back of a length on off, Dhawan does not fiddle with it. Good carry for the bowler there.
Fullish and on off, Dhawan pushes it to the man at covers.

FOUR! Not convincing but India will hope this should get Vijay going. Another good delivery, on a length and around off. It moves away. Vijay goes for the booming drive through the off side, away from his body. He gets an inside edge which goes just past the off pole and into the fine leg fence.

Nicely bowled and again, Vijay does not look very comfertable playing that. It is on middle and it pitched just behind a length. Straightens a touch, Vijay is opened up a touch as he defends it back to the bowler.
Drags his length back and bowls it outside off. No swing on offer. Vijay shoulders his arms to it.
Vijay has not got his timing till now. This is on a fuller length on off, it stops a touch on the in the surface. Vijay tries to drive it through the off side but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
The last one was wide outside off, this is down the leg side. Vijay misses the flick and the keeper moves to his left and collects it.
Bowls this one outside off, Vijay who is one of the best leavers of the ball, does exactly that.

FOUR! A boundary to finish what has been a poor first over by Wafadar. Another ball short and outside off, Dhawan feeds on such deliveries. He rocks back and slaps it through point for the second boundary of the over.
Better by the bowler! On a length around off, slants away from the batsman. Dhawan first thinks of playing at it but then pulls his bat out of the way.
Has not been a good over by Wafadar so far. Once again it is short and wide outside off, Dhawan need not play at those.
FOUR! This time Dhawan makes the bowler pay. Another delivery very short outside off, a lot of width on offer. Dhawan pounces on it and cuts it over point for the first boundary.
This is even wider outside off, Dhawan once again makes a leave.
A loosener to start off with. Short and outside off, Dhawan lets it be.
Wafadar will bowl from the other end.
This is outside off, the batsman need not play at it. End of a good first over by Ahmadzai.

Good delivery! Once again gets the ball to move and troubles the batsman. On a length and around off, this one shapes away after pitching. Vijay has to play at it due to the original line but is beaten by the away movement.
Goes fuller this time around off, it shapes away a touch. Vijay eases it to mid on.
Lands it on a length around off, this one does not move. Vijay defends it solidly.
Once again gets movement into the batsman. It is landed on a length around middle. Dhawan works it towards mid-wicket for a quick run. He gets off the mark.

He bowls it this time and it is a good one. He bowls it on a length around off, it jags back in. Vijay tries to keep it out but gets an inside onto his pads. The ball rolls towards the leg side and the batsmen take the first run of the game. It is signaled as leg bye by the umpire. He might not have spotted in the inside edge.
Anti-climax! False start by the bowler. He comes running in but then pulls out at the last moment. So the wait continues for the first ball.

Done and dusted with the national anthems and we are all set for the game to begin. The sun is out for the  moment and let us hope it stays like this for the whole day. Out come the Afghanistan players and interestingly Mohammad Shahzad is not with the gloves. It is Afsar Zazai who will keep wickets for the away side. They are followed by the two Indian openers, Murali Vijay and Shikhar Dhawan. Yamin Ahmadzai will bowl the first over in Test for Afghanistan. He has three slips and a gully in place. Here we go...
The teams make their way out for the national anthems. The away side will sing its first. Followed by the home team.

Azghar Stanikzai starts by saying it is a proud moment for them. Mentions they too are confident heading into this game and hopes they can end up on the right side. Adds further they do not mind bowling first as he feels there might be some assistance in the first hour. Ends by naming his whole XI.

Ajinkya Rahane says it looks a good wicket to bat on. Mentions they are looking to start well as they are coming on the back of the Indian T20 League. Adds further his side is confident heading into the game and they are well prepared. States it is an honor to represent India as captain. Informs Kuldeep Yadav, Karun Nair, Navdeep Saini and Shardul Thakur miss out.

TOSS - Salim Durani, former Indian all-rounder, provides a memento to the Afghanistan skipper before the toss. Now Rahane tosses the coin, Stanikzai calls it wrong. India win the toss and elect to bat first.

PITCH REPORT - Simon Doull and Sunil Gavaskar say there is grass on the pitch. They reckon it is slightly damp and a lot of movement can be expected. End by saying due to the overcast conditions the captain who wins the toss might want to bowl first.

All eyes will be on the Afghanistan spinners. They have impressed one and all in the shorter formats but can they do it in the longer one? Also it will be interesting to see how their batters pan out. India on the other hand are without their original skipper, Virat Kohli. Ajinkya Rahane will be the stand-in captain. The hosts head into the fixture as heavy favorites but a surprise is something you cannot rule out. Will the Afghans create history by winning their first ever Test or will they be blown away by the Indians? Stay tuned to find out.

The Afghanistan side is moments away from playing their first Test. A big and a very proud moment for them. They will be eager to make an impact right from the start. They however, are up against the number 1 ranked side in Tests, the mighty Indians at M. Chinnaswamy stadium, Bengaluru. Hello and welcome to our coverage.
